basis: Defining cutaneous autoinflammation; hepatitis and fasciitis each reported in 1/1 support hepatic and fascial inflammation. Endocarditis is not established as intrinsic disease; sparse samples.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: endocarditis in 1/1 does not establish intrinsic autoinflammatory cardiac injury; a separately diagnosed infection would not qualify.

basis: Skeletal abnormalities and characteristic macroglossia define the syndrome; renal dysplasia and VSD annotated 80-99%. Hepatosplenomegaly alone does not demonstrate damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: characteristic macroglossia is part of the defining overgrowth phenotype; cleft palate additionally supports structural oral involvement.

basis: Defining pigmentary disease, keratoderma and skin carcinoma; tooth loss and multinodular goiter each occur in 1/2. Conjunctival telangiectasia does not establish functional eye damage.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: multinodular thyroid disease is documented in 1/2 (50%); the supplied phenotype evidence supports structural thyroid involvement, with substantial sampling uncertainty.

basis: Defined by chronic inflammation of labial minor salivary glands and oral lip tissue. Unknown inflammatory cause does not establish immune mediation; associated carcinoma is separate.

decisions.dermatologic: none: the defining lesion concerns labial salivary glands and oral tissue; lip swelling and the skin-disorder parent do not establish independent cutaneous disease.

basis: Cleft palate occurs in 5/9; upper-airway compromise with respiratory insufficiency is annotated 30-79%. Ocular/lacrimal defects also qualify but are omitted at the cap for respiratory severity.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: congenital upper-airway obstruction causes respiratory insufficiency, annotated 30-79%; substantial loss of airway function supports inclusion.
decisions.ocular: none at cap: eyelid coloboma/ptosis occur in 30-79% and lacrimal stenosis in 3/3; qualifying ocular defects yield to more severe respiratory impairment.

basis: Mandatory midbrain-hindbrain malformation defines the umbrella; retinal dystrophy affects approximately 30%. Renal disease (~25%) and hepatic fibrosis remain below threshold across the group.

decisions.ocular: involved: retinal dystrophy causes direct visual-system damage in approximately 30% across Joubert syndrome and related disorders; this is a borderline frequency call.

basis: Craniofacial skeletal defects, microcephaly and congenital heart disease are defining. Cleft palate is a common major structural feature; ear malformations are omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft palate is explicitly a common major structural feature; retained alongside the three defining skeletal, neurologic and cardiac axes.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: midface hypoplasia and other cranial skeletal abnormalities are explicitly part of the defining congenital phenotype.
decisions.otologic: none at cap: common malformed ears are described, but their functional severity is unspecified; major skeletal, brain, cardiac and palatal defects take priority.

basis: Hereditary immune checkpoint dysregulation confers SPTCL/HLH susceptibility. Blood-cell injury and subcutaneous infiltration belong to the separately manifest diseases, not predisposition alone.

decisions.haematologic: none: susceptibility to lymphoma or HLH does not establish blood-cell, marrow or coagulation disease in the predisposition state.

basis: Metopic craniosynostosis defines the skeletal disorder; speech/language developmental delay is reported in 1/1, supporting neurologic dysfunction with substantial sampling uncertainty.

decisions.neurologic: involved: speech/language developmental delay is documented in 1/1; this supports neurologic dysfunction, although the denominator leaves its usual frequency uncertain.

basis: External-ear malformation occurs in 10/10; craniofacial skeletal hypoplasia is defining, with micrognathia in 3/10. Palatal defects in 1/10 fall below the involvement threshold.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: craniofacial skeletal hypoplasia defines craniofacial microsomia; micrognathia in 3/10 corroborates this axis rather than representing a separate complication.
